story.head: The Sabres come in rested
paras: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-3 in Columbus on Oct 1. The Sabres have won two in a row, while the Blue Jackets (5-6-0) lost 3-2 to Carolina on Oct 29. The Blue Jackets played last night, and the Sabres are rested. Going in, the Jackets are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 16th).

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th), have a leaky penalty kill (29th) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). The Sabres, by contrast, get their shots through to the net (2nd). Columbus has scored 2.45 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but don't block many shots (30th). The Sabres have the edge over the Blue Jackets on shots from in close.

Kent Johnson (7 G / 4 A / 11 P in 11 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Charlie Coyle (1 G / 8 A / 9 P in 11 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 13 GP) is next in line.

Jet Greaves (2-4-0 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) will likely start for Columbus. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (3-3-3 / .866 SV% in 8 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Luukkonen has started six of their last ten games, but Ellis got the last one on Oct 29. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
